faq: What is the difference between an MVP and a full app?
An MVP does one job well and leaves out everything else. It is built to answer a question, such as whether people will use or pay for the idea, before you spend on a full product.
Can the MVP grow into the full product later?
Yes. We build on the same React Native setup you would use for a full app, with clean code and your own repository, so later features are added rather than rebuilt.
Do I need a backend for my MVP?
Not always. Basic uses local data. Standard and Premium use a ready-made service such as Firebase or Supabase, which keeps cost and build time low. We pick with you during the planning call.
Who owns the code and the idea?
You do. The code goes in your repository, the accounts are yours and we can sign a simple confidentiality note if you want one before you share details.
desc:
React Native MVP development gives you a focused first version of your app on iOS and Android, built to test your idea with real people. Ecom Swift LLC trims your feature list to one core journey, builds it from one codebase and puts a working app on your phone.

## What is an MVP app?

An MVP, or minimum viable product, is the smallest version of an app that can show whether people want it. It contains one main journey, built properly, and leaves out everything that does not help answer your biggest question.

An MVP is not a rough demo. Testers should be able to install it, sign in if needed, complete the core task and tell you what they think. What it leaves out is scope, not quality.

## Why build an MVP before a full app?

Most app ideas contain assumptions: that people will pay, that they will come back, that a particular feature matters. A full app built on unproven assumptions can use months of budget before anyone confirms them.

An MVP lets you test the riskiest assumption first. If testers use it and ask for more, you know what to build next. If they ignore it, you learn that cheaply and can change direction. Choosing React Native means that learning happens on iPhone and Android together.

## How an MVP affects learning, funding and focus

A working app in testers' hands produces better information than a slide deck. You can see which steps confuse people, which features they ask about and whether they return on day two. That evidence helps decisions about pricing, features and whether to keep going.

It also helps if you talk to investors, partners or early customers, because they can use the product. We cannot promise adoption or revenue, since those depend on your market and idea. What we can do is give you a fast, clean way to find out.

## What a useful MVP includes

- One core journey that proves the main idea from start to finish.
- A short feature cut list, agreed in writing, of what waits for later.
- Clean, simple screens with your brand colors and clear navigation.
- Sign in and a simple database where the idea needs saved data.
- Basic usage tracking, so you can see which screens people use.
- A feedback form inside the app, so testers can tell you what they think.
- Test builds shared by link, with no store listing needed at first.
- Push notifications and one payment or subscription flow in the larger package.
- A store build and listing draft when you are ready to go public.
- A what-to-build-next roadmap based on what you learned.

## What we do

We start with a short call. You describe the idea, the audience and the risk you want to test. Together we cut the feature list until only the core journey remains, and we write it down.

Then we build it. Basic delivers up to a few screens with one working feature and a test build. Standard adds accounts, saved data, tracking, a feedback form and test builds by link. Premium delivers a store-ready first version with a payment or subscription flow, push notifications, store builds and a roadmap. You own the code from the first day.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Name the single question your MVP must answer.
- Recruit a handful of real testers before the build is done.
- Ask testers to complete a task, not just look around.
- Read feedback and tracking data every week.
- Keep a list of ideas for version two, and leave them out of version one.

**Avoid:**
- Copying a rival's feature list without checking that your users want it.
- Polishing small details before the core journey works.
- Testing only with friends who will be polite.
- Treating downloads as proof of demand.
- Spending on marketing before you have seen real usage.

## Who this service is for

A first-time founder with an idea and a small budget. A business owner who wants to try a customer app before committing to a larger project. A product manager who needs a working prototype for user testing and investor conversations.

## What we need from you

A short description of your idea and audience, any sketches or reference apps, and your logo and colors if you have them. We guide you in setting up the accounts you will need. We never need your passwords, and access is shared as a collaborator or developer user.
